answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. Consider a nebula as the anchor of the cost.
